en: The Department of Health officially recognizes lagundi leaves as an effective, safe herbal remedy for relieving coughs and asthma in children.
The government agency PHIVOLCS conducts regular earthquake drills to teach students the practical Duck, Cover, and Hold safety technique.
The National Nutrition Council promotes malunggay leaves as a highly accessible, vitamin-rich local food to prevent childhood malnutrition.
Republic Act 9003 requires every barangay to implement proper solid waste segregation into biodegradable and non-biodegradable bins to prevent disease.
Dr. Fe del Mundo invented a bamboo incubator to provide safe, temperature-controlled care for premature babies in areas without electricity.
Under the Anti-Child Abuse Law, it is a civic duty for every adult to report suspected physical harm against minors.
The Ifugao people maintain ancient rice terraces using traditional stone walls that naturally filter rainwater, ensuring a clean community water supply.
The catastrophic 1991 eruption of Mount Pinatubo led the government to establish modern volcano monitoring stations to warn communities of ashfalls.
Marine scientist Angel Alcala established managed coral reef sanctuaries to ensure sustainable fish populations, securing a safe food source for coastal Filipinos.
The Department of Social Welfare and Development operates the 1388 hotline to provide immediate rescue and safety intervention for abused children.
The Department of Agriculture promotes the orange-fleshed sweet potato, or kamote, as a practical, vitamin-A-rich crop to prevent childhood blindness.
PAGASA issues Tropical Cyclone Wind Signals to warn local government units exactly when to suspend classes and enforce community evacuations.
